subject: NeuraHealth — pilot credits & commit-tier structure
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@neurahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: NeuraHealth pilot credits + commit-tier structure

Alex —

Great to meet on the call today. Per our discussion, I summarized a pragmatic path to run a 6–8 week POC and a subsequent launch ramp with incentives tied to a 3‑month minimum commit. Key points below, attaching a short term sheet (redwood-promo-terms.pdf) and a suggested MOP/test plan (neura-mop-test-plan.xlsx):

- Pilot offer (6–8 weeks): 250k free tokens as evaluation credit + 2 weeks of extended support (priority queue).
- Post-pilot conversion: two commit tiers based on monthly average token consumption over the first 3 months:
  * Tier A (baseline): commit 10M tokens / month — effective rate $0.00075/token.
  * Tier B (ramp): commit 40M tokens / month — effective rate $0.00055/token.
- Launch incentive: for customers that sign Tier B within 30 days of pilot close, we provide a one-time launch credit equal to 10% of the first month’s committed spend (applied as account credit).
- Measurement: tokens measured per API-issued output tokens; prefix caching allowed for deterministic pipelines; discounts apply to billed tokens after credits.
- Term and exit: standard 3‑month minimum then month-to-month; 30‑day notice for downgrades.

A few open items from our side: handling of sensitive PHI in requests (we recommended VPC/private deployment or token redaction), indemnity/limit-of-liability questions for legal, and whether you want the launch credit to be applied to engineering services or purely to API spend.

Attached terms have two optional clauses: an accelerated price ladder if you sustain >150M tokens/month and an overage protection cap for month 1 after launch.

Next steps: if this looks directionally right, I suggest we circulate the term sheet to your procurement and legal, and we (Redwood) will lock the pilot credit and set up a dedicated trial instance.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-promo-terms.pdf (PDF), neura-mop-test-plan.xlsx (Excel)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@neurahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@neurahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeuraHealth pilot credits + commit-tier structure

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we loop in procurement/legal:

1) How are tokens counted for multi-turn conversations where we use your streaming API plus local aggregation? Do the discount tiers apply on total billed tokens per month across endpoints?
2) Is the 250k pilot credit transferable to production if we elect Tier B? Or is it strictly evaluation-only?
3) For the launch credit (10%), can it be paid as an engineering services credit (so we can apply to professional services) rather than API spend?

Also our internal threshold for committing to a paid tier requires a 60 day feature-stability window in production; will Redwood allow a short grace to avoid early penalties if we identify regressions?

If these are straightforward, I’ll share the term sheet with Priya (procurement) and legal to start the procurement timeline.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product, NeuraHealth
alex.turner@neurahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: NeuraHealth pilot credits + commit-tier structure (pricing clarifications)

Forwarding Alex’s clarifying questions — need quick internal alignment so we can give procurement a clean answer. Short answers I propose below; please validate: 

- Token counting: billed tokens = total output tokens from Redwood API (including streaming chunks) + model-internal tokens; discounts apply to the aggregate billed tokens across endpoints on the account. We should be explicit about deterministic counting (we use the same billing meter as hosted customers).
- Pilot credit transferability: allow unused pilot tokens to be converted toward first month of committed spend up to 25% of committed monthly tokens for Tier B only (helps them ramp without losing value).
- Launch credit use-case: allow launch credit to be redeemable against professional services up to 50% (rest must be API spend).
- Grace for regressions: offer a 30-day remediation window without penalties if they report regressions with reproducible evals — after which standard month-to-month billing applies.

Karthik — is the 25% conversion and 50% services carve-out acceptable from a margin perspective? Olga — any legal flags on the remediation window language and transferability?

Thanks — I’m aiming to respond back to Alex within the hour so procurement has time to triage.

—Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: NeuraHealth pilot credits + commit-tier structure (pricing clarifications)

Marissa —

High level: thumbs up on the approach, with two notes: 

1) Financials: the 25% conversion of pilot credit toward month 1 for Tier B is OK if we cap total converted value at $7,500 (keeps downside limited). Also require that the credit conversion triggers only if they sign Tier B within 30 days.
2) Services credit: 50% cap to services is fine but add a clause that services redemption requires pre-approval by our CS lead (to avoid operational write-offs).

If Olga confirms legal, we can send that back. I’ll update the term sheet with the $7.5k cap and procurement trigger.

—Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@neurahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@neurahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeuraHealth pilot credits + commit-tier structure

Alex —

Thanks for the quick questions. Short answers below and attached a one‑page update to the term sheet (redwood-promo-terms.pdf) with the edits inline: 

1) Token counting: billed tokens = total output tokens recorded by Redwood’s hosted meter (includes streaming chunks and model response tokens). All endpoints under the NeuraHealth account aggregate toward the monthly tier volume.

2) Pilot credit conversion: we will allow up to 25% of unused pilot credits to be converted toward the first month of spend if NeuraHealth signs Tier B within 30 days of pilot close. The converted value is capped at $7,500.

3) Launch credit & services: the 10% launch credit can be applied up to 50% against professional services (subject to CS pre-approval), remainder applies to API spend only.

4) Regressions / remediation: we will provide a 30‑day remediation window from the time NeuraHealth documents a reproducible regression with our eval set — no penalties during that window; after remediation period standard billing applies.

If this aligns with your expectations, can Priya confirm procurement will accept (1) the $7.5k conversion cap and (2) CS pre-approval for services redemption? If yes, Olga will prepare a short change order and we’ll share a DocSend/DocuSign link for signatures.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
